# Independent performance review — round 3

Verdict: **PASS for the frozen static scope**. No new blocking performance finding. The two original round-1 P2 findings remain resolved. Compilation, actual tests and runtime performance remain separate pending gates.

Worktree: `/workspace/android-studio-source-providers`; base `ac58815bb268d338bea40a31fff630734cd719f4`; source freeze `review-source-snapshot-round3.json`.

SHA-256 identities:

- generated_artifacts.rs: 5264e4c00d8958a4aaee250c7d924ae89e4665f778b893156442f6af3ed52be0
- project_model.gradle: 508ecc9987932f8d184983f551eca0cb1bc9efa6ed12806dcaff8a0a2f6880b7
- tests/generated_artifacts.rs: 53a4fa7479bf4a7e47c25203207dfb8d19897f73d1a0463d3c947874af11db4a

Verified all 8 frozen source/data hashes, all 184 immutable original guards, 31 cited references and 11 historical planning-probe hashes. Source and original guards matched again before writing this report. Both prior performance reports remain byte-identical: round1 FAIL SHA 7c06b98082d3e3a291eab77adcba8e21ae47f3efdf8b08858d0dfbd37d4f2ef9; round2 static PASS SHA b9cffaa44288070ff56a63b725979e40b3a12639698b7a35fc0ab9e655e9801d. The 28 declared tests were inspected, not executed. The new positional-shape regression covers the envelope and seven nested replacement cases.

## New wrapper assessment

ObjectOnly<D> at generated_artifacts.rs:37 contains the existing deserializer directly. It has no heap-backed field, clone, collection, dynamic trait object, reparsing, serialization-to-JSON intermediary or IO operation. Its deserialize_any at42–46 delegates once to the underlying deserialize_map. The forwarded entry methods at49–53 therefore require an object at the current wire root. Ordinary MapAccess field decoding is provided by the underlying deserializer; scalar, list and nested field contents are not all recursively forced through another wrapper on every byte. Each nested DTO independently enters its own object guard through its Deserialize implementation, which is the intended constant work per object.

The remote Self derives and object_serde implementations at60–72/822–846 direct the existing generated field visitor through that guard, then delegate serialization to the generated serializer. CapturedField<T> likewise forwards its root once. This adds constant dispatch/type-shape checking per DTO or tagged-enum root, with no new retained payload copies. It does not add a repeated traversal of the full model for every nested object. Any buffering intrinsic to Serde's adjacent-tagged enum decoding already existed before the wrapper; the inspected addition creates no extra Value clone or second full-record tree.

The round2-to-round3 source diff changes only the object guard/derive forwarding and related implementations. It leaves the decode/publication/identity algorithms byte-equivalent apart from their shifted locations. The Gradle bridge is byte-identical to round2. Compilation and tests must still verify this generic remote-derive implementation; this static review does not claim that they have done so. No compiler time or executable-size result is inferred from source inspection.

## Preserved static performance properties

- The 16 MiB record check at466–471 still precedes envelope allocation. GeneratedRecord at426–440 retains only generatedArtifacts and preserves present-null versus absent handling. Unrelated Basic data remains ignored by the native field visitor. Sidecar Value ownership moves at478 and is consumed into GeneratedExport at499; no deep clone appears.
- Exact ordered module/directory equality at511–526 precedes paired validation at527. The module join remains O(M), not O(M²). Each collection's ordered-set uniqueness checks remain O(N log N) comparisons and text/path traversal is linear in payload content. No previous cross-module find loop has returned.
- Raw SDK encounter order and duplicate paths remain Vec-based. JAR classpaths remain distinct; there is no sort/dedup conversion of path lists or new filesystem scan. Snapshot creation still moves exported modules and retains only the intended Basic identity copy.
- Path normalization still creates one temporary PathBuf per validated path, proportional to that path's length. No second aggregate normalized-path collection is retained. No app startup hook, UI callback, render work, source discovery or Kotlin inference is added.
- Module task locking, Gradle aggregation and SDK request counts are unchanged because project_model.gradle's SHA is unchanged.

## Unchanged advisories and runtime limits

Duplicate per-module Versions/BasicAndroidProject buildAll requests remain an advisory optimization, with no new measured evidence. JVM canonicalPath costs and same-revision ensure_current identity cloning also remain the round2 advisories; there is still no product hot call site to establish repeated per-row/frame cost. Future query caching/publication checks must preserve independent capability failures, Basic data and raw collection order.

The 16 MiB value remains a wire-input limit, not an allocator/RSS/Gradle-output/JVM serialization cap. The sidecar still uses an intermediate Value and an owned DTO, whose actual peak cost requires a current isolated process measurement. The 600,000-character unrelated payload regression establishes observable decode equivalence only. Historical SDK probe records remain planning evidence, not current gates.

Actual unfiltered AndroidTools tests, strict repository Clippy/format checks, source-matched SDK probes and combined application build/native/full-CI gates remain required under the lead's exclusive leases. No startup latency, responsiveness, memory or large-project timing result is claimed here.

No Cargo, Gradle, app, benchmark, cache mutation, source change or subagent spawn was performed. No test, original fixture, canonical matrix or protected branch was modified. Suggested .rules additions: none.
